findings.description: In contracts/network-policy-export.schema.json line 28, the DNS destination pattern enforces ^(?:\*\.(?=[^.]+\.[^.]+$))?(?:[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?\.)*[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?$. The lookahead (?=[^.]+\.[^.]+$) after *. asserts that following *., the string contains exactly one dot and ends ([^.]+\.[^.]+$). Consequently, wildcards with three or more labels (e.g., *.api.anthropic.com, *.pkg.github.com, *.openai.azure.com) fail schema validation, while only two-label suffixes (e.g., *.example.com) are accepted. SRT requires at least two labels after *. to prevent single-label TLD wildcards (*.com), but allows multi-label domain wildcards. The regex in the contract inadvertently rejects all multi-level subdomain wildcards, causing legitimate vendor endpoint policies to fail export validation and fail closed.
findings.resolution: Update the DNS wildcard lookahead in network-policy-export.schema.json from (?=[^.]+\.[^.]+$) to require at least two labels (e.g. (?=[^.]+(?:\.[^.]+)+$) or (?=[^.]+\..+)), allowing multi-subdomain wildcards while continuing to reject single-label wildcards like *.com.

findings.description: The production process-surface registry and vendor backend migration in design.md:262-264, tasks.md:48-52 (task 4.4), and work-packages.yaml:133-149 (wp-vendor-wiring) enumerate evaluation backends for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi (agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/claude_code.py, codex.py, pi.py), but omit agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/antigravity.py and agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/grok.py. Both antigravity.py (lines 71-77) and grok.py (lines 121-128) directly invoke asyncio.create_subprocess_exec to launch their vendor CLIs (agy and grok). Omitting them leaves two active vendor evaluation backends bypassing the sandbox (violating spec.md:5-7), and will cause the static AST guard in task 4.4 (test_no_vendor_subprocess_bypass.py) to fail in CI on files outside wp-vendor-wiring locked scope.
findings.resolution: Add agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/antigravity.py and agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/grok.py to the process-surface registry in design.md D10, include them in task 4.4, and add them to locks.files and scope.write_allow in wp-vendor-wiring in work-packages.yaml.

findings.description: Package wp-integration in work-packages.yaml violates schema and canonicalization constraints enforced by skills/validate-packages/scripts/validate_work_packages.py: (1) Lines 291-296 declare verification step 2 with kind: manual and command: ..., omitting manual_instructions. The canonical work-packages.schema.json (line 306) strictly requires manual_instructions when kind == manual. (2) Line 271 defines lock key feature:add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement:terminal-integration. Canonical lock key pattern ^feature:[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+:[a-z]+$ (validate_work_packages.py:65) forbids hyphens in the final identifier segment (terminal-integration). Running validate_work_packages.py on work-packages.yaml fails with exit code 1 with both schema and lock_keys validation failures.
findings.resolution: In work-packages.yaml, replace command: with manual_instructions: in wp-integration step 2, and update the lock key in line 271 to a canonical identifier without hyphens in the last segment (e.g. feature:add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement:integration or feature:add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement:terminal).

findings.description: In work-packages.yaml line 256, the verification command for wp-validation-docs invokes skills/.venv/bin/python skills/validate-feature/scripts/linters/dependency_direction.py without arguments. dependency_direction.py requires --skills-root and exits with code 2 when invoked without it (error: the following arguments are required: --skills-root). Because the step asserts expect_exit_code: 0, the wp-validation-docs quality gate will deterministically fail upon execution.
findings.resolution: Update work-packages.yaml line 256 to pass --skills-root skills to dependency_direction.py.

findings.description: Design D1 (design.md:27-33) specifies that routing_context_digest is computed over the complete dg-06 RoutingDispatchContext (including schema_version, decision_id, item_id, phase, attempt, dispatch_work_id, assignment with extensions, and optional provenance), and requires that the backend recomputes and compares it before launch. However, contracts/dispatch-execution-context.schema.json flattens assignment fields into top-level properties, forbids additional properties (additionalProperties: false), and omits provenance. Because DispatchExecutionContext is the only context passed across the dispatch boundary to the backend (PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context), the backend never receives the original dg-06 document or provenance, making pre-launch digest recomputation and comparison impossible.
findings.resolution: Either retain the source dg-06 document structure (or provenance and extension fields) in DispatchExecutionContext, or clarify in D1 and tasks.md that the backend verifies the host-computed digest against the execution context payload rather than independently reconstructing the unprojected dg-06 source document.

findings.description: contracts/sandbox-execution-event.schema.json requires endpoint_digest: ^[a-f0-9]{64}$ (lines 11, 38) and specs/agent-coordinator/spec.md:45 requires endpoint digest (never raw endpoint credentials), whereas DispatchExecutionContext carries base_url (nullable URI). Nowhere in design.md, tasks.md, specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md, or the contracts is endpoint_digest defined: the canonical hash algorithm, the input representation, behavior when base_url is null (e.g., whether endpoint_digest is null or a digest of default endpoints/endpoint_kind), and how the backend maps base_url into endpoint_digest. Without specification, event producers and audit verifiers cannot establish digest parity.
findings.resolution: Define endpoint_digest in design.md D1/D4 and tasks.md task 2.3: specify the exact hashed payload (e.g. normalized base_url or {"endpoint_kind": ..., "base_url": ...} canonical JSON), and specify whether it is null or a stable hash when base_url is null.

findings.description: In design.md:113-114 and specs/agent-coordinator/spec.md:16-17, export ordering is specified as profile before global, priority descending, deny before allow on ties, then policy id ascending. However, existing coordinator database schema 009_network_policies.sql:14 documents priority INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 5, -- lower = higher priority and is_domain_allowed (line 91) orders rules with ORDER BY np.priority ASC. Without inverting priority semantics during migration 044, sorting by priority descending reverses the priority order of existing seed and authored rules, prioritizing default-priority rules over explicit higher-priority rules.
findings.resolution: Clarify rule priority ordering in design.md D4, specs/agent-coordinator/spec.md, and task 2.1: either state that export ordering uses priority ASC matching 009_network_policies.sql (lower number = higher priority), or document that migration 044 maps/inverts priority values.
